# XTRM UI

## Overview

`xtrm-ui` owns XTRM's Pi header, editor density, themes, and tool presentation.
It decorates Pi's native execution rather than replacing tool execution or rewriting
model-facing results.

`custom-footer` is the sole footer owner. `xtrm-ui` never calls `setFooter()`.

## Credits

The original theme palette and header layout were derived from
[pi-dex](https://github.com/mariozechner/lemmy/tree/main/packages/pi-dex) by
[@mariozechner](https://github.com/mariozechner). Write/edit previews are inspired
by **@heyhuynhgiabuu/pi-diff**. The current implementation and theme identifiers
are XTRM-owned; neither project is loaded as UI execution plumbing.

## Themes

The extension discovers four themes:

- `xtrm-dark`
- `xtrm-light`
- `xtrm-dark-flattools`
- `xtrm-light-flattools`

`toolRowBg: false` selects the matching `-flattools` theme. Legacy `pidex-*` values
in Pi settings or persisted session preferences are migrated to the equivalent
`xtrm-*` value.

## Tool Rendering

The resting view is a compact execution timeline: one line per tool call, with
the full result behind expansion. A row states what happened, not how much was
produced.

```text
Thinking  Inspecting the renderer and identifying the relevant files
  Ran shell command  pnpm test  12 failed, 84 passed  2.4s
  read  packages/pi-extensions/extensions/xtrm-ui/index.ts:1-40
  used codemode  x = 1  ok  42ms  ↗
● Updated the renderer and added regression tests.
```

Each surface keeps its own wording — native shell rows say `Ran shell command`,
other native rows start with the tool name, external rows say `used <provider>`
— and shares the same three-step weight ladder
(`packages/pi-extensions/shared/weight.ts`), never a raw bold call:

| Tier | Encoding | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `heavy` | bold + `muted` | one identity per row (wake cards), error verbs |
| `semi` | `muted`, no bold | tool verbs and tool names |
| `soft` | `dim` | subjects, outcomes, durations, chrome |

Colour carries meaning, not decoration. The ladder is grayscale; red marks
failure at full strength (never dimmed, always also the word `failed`), amber
marks activity, and the theme accent marks thinking. Provider badges stay in
expanded external frames.

Expansion uses two distinct bindings: `Ctrl+O` for tool output and `Ctrl+T` for
thinking. Neither is advertised on a resting row. A row that hides a substantial
payload (three or more lines) ends with `↗`; nothing else carries a hint.

Native tools (`bash`, `read`, `write`, `edit`, `grep`, `find`, `ls`) and external
tools (Serena, GitNexus, structured-return, process, generic) share this grammar.
Expanded rows keep the complete payload: bash keeps its output tree, edit and
write keep the 18-line diff, external frames keep the provider badge. Rendering
never mutates tool-result payloads.

`ultracompact` is on by default; `/xtrm-ui-ultra off` restores the multi-line
frame. Preview caps stay independent per section (`commandPreviewLines`,
`extPreviewLines`) so a long program never starves its output.

## Thinking Rows

Collapsed: `Thinking` plus one clause (64 characters maximum), italic, in the
theme accent hue with the label at full strength and the recap one faint step
down. The hue is what separates thinking from the grayscale tool rows. No
character count and no inline shortcut. Expanded: the full trace behind `Ctrl+T`,
with the collapse hint shown only in that state.

## Preferences

Only active, user-controlled behavior is persisted:

| Preference | Default | Command |
|---|---|---|
| `themeName` | `xtrm-dark` | `/xtrm-ui-theme dark\|light` |
| `density` | `compact` | `/xtrm-ui-density compact\|comfortable` |
| `showHeader` | `true` | `/xtrm-ui-header on\|off` |
| `forceTheme` | `true` | `/xtrm-ui-forcetheme on\|off` |
| `toolRowBg` | `false` | `/xtrm-ui-rowbg on\|off` |
| `commandPreviewLines` | `4` | `/xtrm-ui-command-lines <1-50>` |
| `resultPreviewLines` | `6` | `/xtrm-ui-result-lines <1-50>` |
| `diffPreviewLines` | `18` | `/xtrm-ui-diff-lines <1-50>` |
| `extPreviewLines` | `6` | `/xtrm-ui-ext-lines <1-50>` |
| `extNoCompact` | `false` | `/xtrm-ui-ext-compact on\|off` |
| `ultracompact` | `true` | `/xtrm-ui-ultra on\|off` |

Tool rows start collapsed. Hidden thinking blocks use an empty placeholder. These are
fixed presentation choices rather than persisted preferences.

## Commands

| Command | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `/xtrm-ui` | Show active preferences, model, and context usage |
| `/xtrm-ui-theme dark\|light` | Switch the XTRM theme family |
| `/xtrm-ui-density compact\|comfortable` | Change editor horizontal padding |
| `/xtrm-ui-header on\|off` | Toggle the XTRM header |
| `/xtrm-ui-forcetheme on\|off` | Enable or disable XTRM theme ownership |
| `/xtrm-ui-rowbg on\|off` | Toggle native tool-row backgrounds |
| `/xtrm-ui-ultra on\|off` | Toggle the one-line timeline (multi-line frame when off) |
| `/xtrm-ui-reset` | Restore the five defaults above |

Obsolete result-compaction and external-chrome commands are intentionally not
registered. External tools always use the unified background renderer.

## Install and Migration

Canonical source lives under `packages/pi-extensions/` and is exposed by the
managed `@jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions` package. Before Pi reads its configured theme,
launch preflight symlinks the four XTRM-owned theme files into `~/.pi/agent/themes`.
The extension still discovers its package-local theme directory after startup.

Runtime sync removes the obsolete UI package entry. It migrates legacy theme names
and removes the retired `xtrmExternalCompact` setting in project settings; user-global
preferences are migrated only during global runtime sync. Unrelated Pi settings remain
unchanged.
